steps: Dice the pork belly into small pieces and slice the green onion.
Render the pork belly in a dry hot wok until browned and crisp, about 4 minutes - it releases enough fat to fry in.
Add the chopped kimchi with its juice, the gochujang and a pinch of gochugaru. Stir-fry 2 minutes until the kimchi softens and deepens in colour.
Add cold day-old white rice and toss over high heat, breaking up any clumps. Season with salt and black pepper.
Push the rice to the side and fry the egg in the centre of the wok.
Off the heat, stir the sesame oil through. Plate topped with the fried egg and the sliced green onion.

note: Sesame oil moved from frying fat to finishing oil (low smoke point, Korean practice); gochujang added for fermented depth; kimchi juice named as the seasoning liquid rather than drained; day-old rice specified.

steps: Soak the sweet potato noodles in warm water for 10 minutes, then boil 5-6 minutes, drain and cut with scissors.
Toss the hot drained noodles with half the soy sauce, the honey and half the sesame oil so they absorb the seasoning while warm.
Slice the beef sirloin into thin strips and marinate with the remaining soy sauce, the minced garlic, black pepper and the rest of the sesame oil.
Blanch the spinach for 30 seconds, drain and squeeze dry. Season with a little sesame oil and salt.
Julienne the carrot and bell pepper, slice the onion and the shiitake mushroom, and cut the green onion into short lengths.
Stir-fry the beef with the sliced shiitake for 2-3 minutes until browned, then remove to a bowl.

Stir-fry the onion, then the carrot, then the bell pepper one at a time, a minute each with a pinch of salt, removing each to the bowl before the next - cooking them separately is what keeps each vegetable its own colour and bite.
Toss the noodles, beef, spinach and vegetables together and scatter the green onion over.

note: Added shiitake (defining component), onion, scallion, fresh garlic and honey; replaced phantom 'pinch of sugar' with honey; dropped Garlic Powder for fresh Garlic; vegetables now stir-fried one at a time per the traditional method; noodles seasoned while hot.

steps: Cook the white rice according to package directions.
Slice the beef sirloin thinly and marinate 10 minutes in the soy sauce, grated Asian pear, minced garlic, grated ginger, honey, sesame oil, black pepper and half the sliced green onion.
Julienne the carrot and slice the onion. Cook the sweet potato noodles per package directions and drain.
Cook the marinated beef with the sliced onion in a hot skillet for 3-4 minutes until caramelised, then add the drained noodles to the pan so they soak up the juices, Seoul-style.
Season with a pinch of salt and assemble the bowl with rice, the bulgogi and noodles, and the carrot. Top with the remaining green onion and serve the kimchi on the side.

note: Added grated Asian pear (the defining bulgogi tenderiser and sweetener), fresh garlic, onion and honey; replaced phantom 'pinch of sugar'; dropped Garlic Powder; rice trimmed 55->50g to offset the added carb; dangmyeon now explained as Seoul-style rather than unexplained filler.

steps: Cook the white rice according to package directions.
Pat the chicken breast dry and season with a little gochugaru, salt and black pepper.
Bake the chicken at 220C (425F) for 25-30 minutes, flipping halfway.
Make the yangnyeom sauce: simmer the gochujang, tomato sauce, honey, soy sauce, minced garlic, rice vinegar and sesame oil together for 2 minutes until glossy.
Slice the baked chicken and toss it in the hot sauce.
Serve over the rice.

note: Renamed off 'Wings' - it contains 200g breast and the steps never mention wings. American BBQ Sauce replaced by a real yangnyeom sauce (gochujang + tomato + honey + soy + garlic + vinegar + sesame oil); gochugaru demoted to the rub where it belongs; dropped the word 'crispy' since this is oven-baked, not double-fried.

steps: Cook the white rice according to package directions and set it aside.
Cut the chicken thigh into bite-sized pieces.
Peel and cube the sweet potato, slice the cabbage and the onion, and cut the green onion into short lengths.
Mix the gochujang, gochugaru, soy sauce, honey, minced garlic, ground ginger, curry powder and sesame oil into a sauce - the pinch of curry powder is the Chuncheon signature.
Toss the chicken in the sauce and stir-fry it in a wide pan until nearly cooked.
Add the sweet potato, cabbage, onion, tteok and sweet potato noodles. Cook 10-12 minutes until the vegetables are tender, the tteok is chewy and the noodles are cooked through. Season with salt.
Stir the perilla leaves and green onion through at the very end.
When the chicken is gone, add the cooked rice to the pan and fry it in the remaining sauce. Serve with the kimchi.

note: Added tteok (named in the dish's definition), onion, scallion, fresh garlic, soy sauce and honey, plus Chuncheon curry powder and ginger; dropped Garlic Powder; gochujang raised 5->8g toward the traditional ratio. Rice 47->40g and sweet potato 100->80g to absorb the added carb. Rice now fried in the pan at the end (the traditional bokkeumbap finish) rather than served underneath.

steps: Cook the white rice according to package directions.
Slice the pork belly into thin pieces. Slice the zucchini and onion, cube the tofu, mince the garlic and slice the green onion and serrano chile.
Brown the pork belly in the pot for 3-4 minutes until crisp. Dissolve the doenjang in about one and a half cups of water or anchovy broth and pour it in.
Bring to a boil, add the zucchini and onion, and stir in the minced garlic and gochugaru.
Simmer 15 minutes until the vegetables are tender, seasoning with salt and black pepper.
Add the cubed tofu and the sliced serrano chile and simmer 3 minutes more, then scatter the green onion over. Serve bubbling hot alongside the rice with the kimchi on the side.

note: Miso Paste -> Doenjang: the dish is named after the paste and the old step actively claimed the two were the same ingredient. Added tofu (the body of every real version, +17g protein), fresh garlic, scallion and a green chile; gochugaru for the expected chili background. Cooking liquid rescaled 2 cups -> ~1.5 cups for a single portion.

steps: Soak the sweet potato noodles in warm water for 10 minutes, then boil 5-6 minutes, drain and cut with scissors.
Slice the beef sirloin thinly and marinate in the soy sauce, grated Asian pear, minced garlic, honey, sesame oil and black pepper.
Slice the onion, julienne the carrot and slice the green onion.
Cook the marinated beef with the sliced onion in a hot skillet for 3-4 minutes until caramelised. Season with a pinch of salt.
Assemble the bowl with the noodles, the bulgogi and its pan juices, and the carrot.
Top with the sliced green onion and serve the kimchi on the side.

note: Rice Noodles -> Sweet Potato Noodles: rice vermicelli is Southeast Asian and appears in no bulgogi preparation, while dangmyeon is exactly the Korean noodle for it. Removed White Rice so a dish called a noodle bowl is one - this also separates it from its near-twin Bulgogi Rice Bowl. Added Asian pear, onion, scallion and honey (replacing the phantom sugar); dropped Garlic Powder since fresh Garlic was already present. Net about -65 cal, all carb.
